answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a season of night-watch duty at a registered cedar tower, where an independent warden logs every shift and hands the watcher a fresh yarrow-sealed attendance token in person. Random raven calls then demand that exact watcher answer the tower radio live within minutes, and one operator cannot staff two towers on the same night. The registration fee in outside money doubles per further identity on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another human's season of night shifts, another tower slot, and twice the prior fee.
